findings.headline: Separate choices within one legislative episode
findings.compact: Foushee opposed passage of that complete House proposal; no preferred alternative or separate component position is established. Selected House H.R. 1 provisions would fund border infrastructure and detention, set fiscal 2025 asylum filing/pending fee floors of $1,000/$100 and specified asylum/parole/TPS employment-authorization initial/renewal fee floors of $550, and limit those documents to at most six months. This is a whole-package passage choice, with qualifications. Foushee opposed concurrence in that complete Senate replacement; no preferred alternative or separate component position is established. Selected Senate H.R. 1 provisions would fund border infrastructure and detention, set fiscal 2025 asylum filing/pending fee floors of $100 each and specified asylum/parole/TPS employment-authorization initial/renewal fee floors of $550/$275, with distinct duration and termination rules. This is a whole-replacement concurrence choice, with qualifications.
detail: Foushee opposed passage of that complete House proposal; no preferred alternative or separate component position is established.

This May22 House passage is the whole H.R.1 reconciliation package, not a separate immigration-only vote. The controlling House choice uses H.Res.436: Rules Committee Print119-3 modified by the amendment printed in H.Rept.119-113 was considered adopted. The retained Immigration clauses are reconstructed against that chain and the contemporaneous as-amended floor Record. The currently served EH incorporates later corrections and renumbering and is a comparison witness for these unchanged selected clauses, not the controlling entire vote-time text. Later engrossment corrections and the July Senate replacement are not silently substituted for this choice. The description selects border infrastructure, detention, State reimbursement and asylum-fee mechanisms; it does not inventory every immigration-related tax, benefit, employment-authorization, child-sponsor or removal provision in this multi-domain package. Section60001 would make additional fiscal2025 CBP appropriations available until September30,2029: $46.5billion for primary/waterborne/secondary barriers, access roads and associated detection attributes; a separate $50million for specified invasive plants impeding RioGrande border operations; and $5billion for CBP facilities/checkpoints near the southwest, northern and maritime borders. These are different purposes, not one immigration-enforcement account or actual expenditures. The adopted manager amendment adds section60004: $12billion in additional fiscal2025 DHS funds, available until September30,2029, for grants reimbursing States for costs of actions on or after January21,2021 assisting federal border/immigration enforcement, including detention/removal and combating unlawful entry of persons/contraband. Applications need satisfactory cost evidence, and DHS cannot reimburse a State already reimbursed under another DHS grant program. This is funding subject to a process and conditions, not proof of State awards or a newly conferred State removal power. Section70101 would appropriate an additional $45billion for fiscal2025 to ICE, available until September30,2029, solely for single-adult alien detention and family residential-center capacity. DHS MAY detain family units pending a removal decision and, if ordered removed, until removal. Its family-center definition includes accompanied alien children, excludes unaccompanied alien children, and expressly applies regardless of State/local facility licensing. Its single-adult detention standards clause says they shall be set in the Secretary's SOLE discretion. Preserve that printed language without importing the Senate's express consistent-with-applicable-law qualification or deciding its interaction with judicial/other legal constraints. The existing unaccompanied-child definition in6USC279(g)(2) requires no lawful immigration status, age under18, and no US parent/legal guardian or none available for care/physical custody; childhood alone does not establish that category. Capacity funding and permission are not a universal detention mandate, removal order or actual detention outcome. Section70002 would require an additional fee at the time an alien files an asylum application: the fiscal2025 amount may be set by rule but cannot be less than $1,000. It cannot be waived/reduced. From fiscal2026 its amount increases using the prior fiscal-year fee and the printed July-to-July CPI-U increase, with the increment rounded down to a multiple of $10. Half of the Attorney-General-filed receipts go to EOIR; half of DHS-filed receipts go to USCIS's existing Immigration Examinations Fee Account; those credited amounts may be retained/spent without further appropriation, and the remainder goes to Treasury. Section70010 separately requires a fee for EACH CALENDAR YEAR an application remains pending, initially at least $100 for fiscal2025, with later CPI-U adjustment, Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction. Its printed adjustment has no express rounding term; the filing-fee rounding rule is not copied into it. These are separate filing and pending-application charges, not fixed lifetime amounts or a claim that every asylum applicant actually paid. Section70023 changes existing INA208(d)(3)/8USC1158(d)(3) from MAY impose fees to SHALL, strikes the following cost-cap/installment/nonmandatory-fee language and preserves authority to set additional adjudication/naturalization fees under286(m). The existing paragraph already allowed fees for asylum consideration, employment authorization and asylum-based adjustment and capped them at adjudication costs; the bill does not create first-ever fee authority or establish a new substantive asylum eligibility test through that edit. Existing1356(m)/(n) supply the account/cost-recovery context. Employment-authorization provisions are separate from asylum filing and annual pending-application fees. House70003 would charge an additional fee on initial employment-authorization applications for asylum applicants underINA208(d)(2), paroled aliens and applicants underTPS244(a)(1)(B). Each initial fee has a fiscal2025 floor of$550, may be higher by DHS rule, cannot be waived/reduced and has the printed fiscal2026-onward July-to-July CPI-U increment rounded down to$10. All three initial authorizations would last no more than six months. In70003(a)(4), the House allocation sentence says25percent of fees received UNDER THIS SECTION goes to USCIS's existing fee account to retain/spend without further appropriation, with50percent of that credited amount for benefit-fraud detection/prevention; uncredited amounts go to Treasury. The separately printed parole/TPS subsections direct their fees to Treasury. Preserve those exact scope words rather than silently deciding their interaction. House70012 and70014 separately impose additional parole/TPS employment-authorization renewal or extension fees with fiscal2025$550floors, possible higher rule amounts, subsequent CPI increments rounded down to$10, Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction. Both initial and renewed/extended authorizations in those sections last no more than six months. House70013 imposes at least$550 for each asylum-based renewal/extension, Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction; that section prints no annual inflation formula. DHS MAY provide asylum-applicant employment authorization for at most six months, and each renewal/extension also has that limit. Authorization terminates immediately after an asylum-officer denial unless referred to an immigration judge;30days after an immigration-judge denial unless timely appealed to BIA; or immediately after BIA denies an appeal of asylum denial. After such termination DHS cannot grant, renew or extend it unless a FederalCourtOfAppeals remands to BIA. This restriction concerns employment authorization, not an automatic asylum denial, immediate removal or a bar on all judicial review. The pre-vote1158(d)(2) already says asylum applicants are not entitled to employment authorization but it may be provided by regulation; applicants not otherwise eligible cannot receive it before180days after asylum filing. Existing1254a(a)(1)(B)/(a)(2) authorizes employment and makes work authorization effective throughout TPS. Fee/document-validity provisions do not themselves end TPS, create first work authority or establish everyone's eligibility. The existing parole paragraph1182(d)(5)(A)/(B) is case-by-case urgent-humanitarian/significant-public-benefit authority subject to the printed statutory exceptions, including the refugee qualification and does not constitute admission. These fees do not supply a grant of parole or automatic employment permission. House70007 imposes a separate additional sponsor-placement fee, collected by HHS from the individual BEFORE placing an unaccompanied alien child underTVPRA235(c). Its fiscal2025 floor is$3,500 or a higher rule amount, with fiscal2026-onward July-to-July CPI-U increments rounded down to$10 and no waiver/reduction. The stated purpose is partial reimbursement for the child's prior federal-custody processing, housing, food, education, transport and other care.25percent goes to HHS to retain/spend without further appropriation for sponsor/adult-household background checks; the remainder goes to Treasury. The specified checks include names, SSNs, dates of birth, validated residence, immigration status and contact information for the sponsor and all adult household residents, and records checks including sex-offender registry, public-records background and fingerprint-based national criminal history. Existing1232(c) already requires protective/suitability assessments, identity/relationship verification, independent risk findings and home studies in specified cases. This is not first-ever sponsor vetting or a new assertion that any sponsor has criminal activity. House70020 imposes ANOTHER additional sponsor fee BEFORE the unaccompanied child's release to the sponsor. Its fiscal2025 floor is$5,000 or a higher rule amount with later CPI increments rounded down to$10, Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction. Despite its failure-to-appear title, collection is not conditioned on a child already missing court or having an in-absentia order. At the end of the child's immigration proceedings as an unaccompanied child OR at the end of that sponsorship, HHS MAY reimburse if the sponsor demonstrates the child was not ordered removed in absentia. If such an order was rescinded underINA240(b)(5)(C), the sponsor MAY SEEK reimbursement. Neither reimbursement pathway is an automatic refund. The two sponsor fees remain distinct additional charges; there is no claim that every applicant actually paid them or that payment establishes suitability. Existing1232(c) placement protections and279(g)(2) UAC definition remain material context; their interaction with fee collection is not a finding of actual placement, detention or legal enforceability. House70021 requires a separate fiscal2025 fee of at least$5,000, possibly higher by rule, on an alien BOTH ordered removed in absentia under1229a(b)(5) AND subsequently arrested by ICE. It has later CPI increments rounded down to$10, Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction, and does not apply if the underlying order was rescinded under1229a(b)(5)(C). House70022 separately charges any INADMISSIBLE alien at the time CBP apprehends the person BETWEEN PORTS OF ENTRY; its fiscal2025 floor is$5,000 or higher by rule, later CPI increments rounded down to$10, Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction. Do not treat every arrest, port-of-entry encounter, unadmitted person or failure to attend court as satisfying these exact fee predicates. The complete pre-vote1229a(b)(5) and(e) retain the written-notice rule and failure-to-provide-address exception, clear/unequivocal/convincing evidence of notice and removability, and separate rescission routes: a motion within180days showing exceptional circumstances beyond the alien's control, or at any time for missing statutory notice or no-fault failure while in federal/state custody. Filing those motions stays removal pending the immigration judge's disposition. Exceptional circumstances include the specified battery/extreme cruelty or serious illness/death examples, excluding less compelling circumstances; removability distinguishes inadmissibility for an unadmitted alien from deportability for an admitted alien.1229(a) preserves notice/address/change-of-hearing context. The fee provisions do not themselves create an in-absentia order, repeal rescission, establish a new removal ground or prove an individual enforcement outcome. House70004 adds a parole-entry fee with fiscal2025floor$1,000 or a higher DHS rule amount, fiscal2026-onward July-to-July CPI-U increments rounded down to$10, Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction for an applicable fee. It applies to each alien paroled into the US EXCEPT where the alien establishes one of the printed parole-reason exceptions; fee exceptions are not erased by the separate waiver bar. The fee exceptions retain their actual predicates: a medical emergency with necessary treatment unavailable in the foreign state where the alien resides OR a life-threatening emergency with insufficient normal-visa time; the parent/legal guardian of such a medical-emergency MINOR; the alien needed in the US to donate an organ or tissue for transplant, with insufficient normal-visa time; a close family member in the United States whose death is imminent, when normal visa processing would prevent arriving while that person is alive; or seeking to attend a close family member's funeral, when normal visa processing would prevent arriving in the United States in time for it; an adopted child's urgent treatment needed before expected final adoption-related visa issuance while in the petitioner's legal custody; a LAWFUL INA245 adjustment applicant returning after temporary travel abroad; and a person returned to a contiguous country under235(b)(2)(C) paroled to attend the person's immigration hearing. The law-enforcement significant-public-benefit exception requires a DHS determination that significant public benefit has resulted or will result from the parole, BOTH assistance to the USGovernment AND presence required in that matter, PLUS at least one of inadmissibility, failure to meet nonimmigrant-admission eligibility, or insufficient normal-visa time; it is not every asserted public benefit. House exception9 separately requires a Cuban national LIVING IN CUBA, an approvedINA203(a) petition, no immediately available immigrant visa, all immigrant-visa eligibility requirements, no other inadmissibility AND a parole grant furthering the printed US minimum-annual-legal-migration commitment under the1994/1995Cuba-USagreements. Existing1153(a) identifies family-preference visa classes; that eligibility context does not prove approval, visa availability or an actual grant. This is not an exemption for every Cuban national, every parolee or the differently printed Senate Cuban/Haitianentrant category. Existing1182(d)(5) parole authority remains subject to its printed humanitarian/public-benefit/case-by-case/statutory-exception terms and non-admission distinction; a fee or exception does not confer parole, adjustment, admission or hearing outcome. House70005 adds a separate SIJ application fee with fiscal2025floor$500 or a higher rule amount, later CPI increments rounded down to$10, Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction. The fee predicate requires that reunification with ONEparent or legal guardian is viable despite abuse/neglect/abandonment or a similar State-law basis making reunification with the OTHERparent/legalguardian not viable. It is not stated as a fee on every SIJ applicant or an amendment creating SIJ status. Complete1101(a)(27)(J) already requires the specified USjuvenile-court dependency/custody determination and nonviable reunification with1ORboth parents on the listed State-law bases, a best-interest finding against return to the identified former country, and DHSconsent; HHS-specific custody-jurisdiction consent and no derived rights by virtue of parentage remain. Do not substitute nonimmigrantJexchange-visitor provisions, infer a UAC-under18 rule, grant status from a fee, or assume that paying changes parental rights. House70006 adds a separate TPS-consideration fee with fiscal2025floor$500 or a higher rule amount, later CPI increments rounded down to$10, Treasury disposition and no waiver/reduction. Its status predicate is an alien NOTADMITTED to the US OR an admitted NONIMMIGRANT who at TPSapplication time failed to maintain/extend the applicable nonimmigrant status (including authorized-stay compliance) OR comply with its conditions. It is not an undifferentiated fee on every TPSapplicant, an EADfee, or proof of inadmissibility/criminal conduct. The pre-vote1254a(c)(1)(B) already permits a reasonable registration fee capped$50 and a separate additional work-document fee for post-July17,1991designations, with appropriation-credit language. This House fee is ADDITIONAL to other authorized fees; the separately stated registration cap is not described as a newly created TPS application right or the House newfee's ceiling. Other TPSeligibility/work-authorization protections remain; fee liability does not establish status eligibility or an actual collection. House 70008 adds a visa-integrity fee on each alien issued a nonimmigrant visa, collected upon issuance in addition to other authorized fees. The fiscal 2025 minimum is $250 or a higher DHS rule amount; fiscal 2026 onward adds the July-to-July CPI-U increment rounded down to the next lowest multiple of $1. Unreimbursed fees go to Treasury; the applicable fee cannot be waived or reduced. DHS MAY reimburse after the visa period of validity expires if the alien demonstrates ONE of three printed alternatives: did not seek admission during that validity period; OR after admission complied with ALL visa conditions, including no unauthorized employment, AND departed no later than five days after the date authorized to remain in the US; OR FILED to extend, change or adjust status within the visa validity period. Filing is the printed third alternative, not a required grant; nonuse is its own first alternative. Reimbursement is discretionary and qualified, not an automatic refund or a new permission to stay or work. Visa validity and authorized stay are not interchangeable, and the reimbursement departure condition is not described as a general grace period. The pre-vote 1101(a)(26) definition identifies a visa properly issued to an eligible nonimmigrant by a competent officer; issuance does not itself prove admission, compliance or reimbursement. House 70009 separately adds a fee on ANY alien applying for Form I-94, with fiscal 2025 minimum $24 or a higher DHS rule amount, later July-to-July CPI-U increments, no expressly printed increment-rounding rule, and no waiver/reduction. Twenty percent of each collected application fee is deposited pursuant to existing 1356(q)(2) and available to CBP to retain and spend without further appropriation for Form I-94 processing; the remainder goes to Treasury. The existing Land Border Inspection Fee Account was already established, including I-94/I-94W/I-68 and similar land-port receipts. The new section says any alien applying for the form; the account name does not narrow that application predicate to land ports. Existing subsection (q)(3) refunds appropriations for inspection expenses, not the applicant, and is not described as a personal fee-refund entitlement. No fee amount proves an actual application, collection, admission or immigration-status outcome. House 70017 amends the existing ESTA fee, rather than creating the travel-authorization System or treating it as admission. Pre-vote 1187(h)(3) already specifies an initial fee comprising $17 per travel authorization plus an amount at least sufficient to recover full System provision/administration costs. The proposal adds a $10 MINIMUM to that cost-recovery component while retaining the full-cost condition, and adds another component of at least $13. These are components of the existing sum, not an undifferentiated $10 or $13 total fee. It limits annual deposits from the existing $17 component into the Travel Promotion Fund to not more than $20 million, sending that component's remainder to Treasury; it expressly sends the new $13 component to Treasury. The existing administration-cost component remains transferred to Treasury and available for administering the System. The sunset edit extends only the existing clause(i)(I) Travel Promotion Fund fee restriction from fiscal years beginning after October31,2028 to those beginning after October31,2034. Fiscal2026-onward CPI-U adjustment expressly names clause(i)(II), but its prior-year base literally says the amount imposed UNDER THIS SUBSECTION. The full-cost component/subsection-base relationship is preserved for application review, not silently rewritten as a CPI adjustment of an isolated $10 amount or the whole total; no increment-rounding rule is printed here. The complete pre-vote System/validity limits distinguish eligible travel from admissibility and distinguish denial of ESTA travel eligibility from denial of visa eligibility. The selected ESTA amendment prints no new express fee-waiver prohibition; none is imported from EVUS, and waiver availability is not inferred. House 70018 separately edits the existing immigration inspection/preinspection user fee in 1356(d). Its collection event remains inspection of each passenger arriving at a US port, or preinspection outside the US before arrival, aboard a COMMERCIAL aircraft or vessel. The existing $7 becomes a fiscal2025 MINIMUM of $10, with later July-to-July CPI-U increments rounded down to the next lowest $0.25 and a no-waiver/reduction clause. It expressly makes (d) subject to the retained (e) exceptions. The old non-aircraft geographical-origin exemption for Canada/Mexico/the US/adjacent islands is removed; the separate $3 commercial-vessel-origin charge is replaced with an exemption from (d) for IMMIGRATION INSPECTION AT DESIGNATED PORTS OF ENTRY of passengers arriving either by the separately defined ferry or by the specified Great Lakes vessels. A passenger in transit to an outside-US destination AND receiving no immigration inspection remains exempt. The printed ferry definition remains: a vessel outside ocean/coastwise service, providing only deck-passenger and/or vehicle capacity, a short frequent run along the most direct water route, and a public bridge/tunnel-type service. The Great Lakes branch retains its Great Lakes/connecting-waterway and regular-schedule conditions. These own predicates are not transferred between exception branches, and the fee is not described as applying to every border crossing or every inadmissible person. The new clause directs $1 per inspected/preinspected individual to Treasury; unstruck 1356(h)(1)(A) separately says ALL (d) receipts enter the Immigration User Fee Account notwithstanding other provisions. Both printed provisions and the account's appropriations-refund framework remain visible for application review, without inventing a resolved residual distribution or personal refund right. House 70019 adds an EVUS fee at enrollment for an alien SUBJECT to that System, in addition to other authorized fees. Fiscal2025 minimum is $30 or a higher DHS rule amount; later CPI-U increments round down to $0.25 and the fee cannot be waived or reduced. It establishes a separate CBP EVUS Account; fees enter that account LESS $5 PER ENROLLMENT directed to Treasury. Account deposits are appropriated without further appropriation and available until expended for CBP costs administering EVUS. The collection event, quarter-dollar increment and fixed Treasury deduction are distinct from ESTA or the commercial-passenger inspection fee; no new System eligibility, admission, visa grant, compliance determination or actual collection follows from the fee. House 70011 adds a fee for EACH continuance that an alien BOTH REQUESTS and IS GRANTED by an immigration judge. The fiscal2025 minimum is $100 or a higher AttorneyGeneral rule amount, with fiscal2026-onward July-to-July CPI-U increments and no expressly printed increment-rounding rule. Fees go to Treasury. The no-waiver/reduction clause preserves a separate NO-FEE exception when the requested continuance is granted BASED ON the defined exceptional circumstances. Complete pre-vote1229a(e)(1), the section240 definition, requires circumstances BEYOND THE ALIEN'S CONTROL and excludes less compelling circumstances. Its examples are illustrative, not an exclusive list: battery/extreme cruelty to the alien or the alien's child/parent; serious illness of the alien; or serious illness/death of the alien's spouse/child/parent. Those own person/event predicates are not collapsed into any family illness/death, and ordinary good cause or a continuance request alone is not described as satisfying the statutory fee exception. The proposal does not charge a denied request merely because it was filed, turn the exception into a fee waiver, or establish an actual grant or exceptional-circumstances finding. House 70015 separately adds fees for two different diversity-visa events: filing a diversity immigrant-visa application ($400 fiscal2025 minimum or higher DHS rule amount, collected at filing) and registering for that program ($250 minimum or higher rule amount, collected at registration). Both have fiscal2026-onward July-to-July CPI-U increments; ONLY the application increment expressly rounds down to$10, while the registration formula prints no rounding rule. Both applicable fees cannot be waived or reduced. Across fees received under this SECTION, 10percent is directed to detecting/preventing program fraud and offsetting program costs, and a separate10percent is credited to ICE to retain/spend without further appropriation for detention, immigration enforcement and removal operations; amounts not used or credited go to Treasury. These are not percentages of only one fee or assumed actual expenditure. Complete pre-vote1153(c) already establishes diversity visa allocation, including its five-year admission/geographic formulas, high-admission-state exclusion, regional redistribution and seven-percent state limit, and the education OR qualified-work-experience requirement. The proposal adds fees to the identified program rather than creating it, changing those allocation/eligibility rules by payment, guaranteeing selection or issuing a visa. Registration, application, selection and actual grant remain distinct; no separate component preference follows from either member's whole-package vote. House 70016 adds ten EOIR court/application/appeal/motion fee provisions. In(a)-(c), an alien's court filing OR court adjudication of the identified adjustment, inadmissibility-waiver orTPS application triggers payment at filing OR, as applicable, before court adjudication; two automatic charges for the same application are not asserted. The(d)/(e) alien appeals, (f) practitioner appeal and(g) alien motion collect at filing. The(h)-(j) provisions collect when an alien files the identified suspension, permanent-resident cancellation or nonpermanent-resident cancellation/adjustment application WITH AN IMMIGRATION COURT. House(j) identifies the application for certain nonpermanent residents without copying Senate's distinct non-LPR-payer wording. The ten listed fiscal2025 floors are separate fee events, additional to other authorized fees, with a higher AttorneyGeneral rule amount permitted: adjustment to lawful permanent residence $1,500; waiver of grounds of inadmissibility $1,050; TPS $500; appeal from an immigration-judge decision $900; appeal from a DHS-officer decision $900; practitioner disciplinary appeal $1,325; motion to reopen or reconsider an immigration-judge or Board of Immigration Appeals decision $900; suspension of deportation application $600; cancellation of removal for the specified permanent-resident category $600; and cancellation/adjustment for the specified nonpermanent-resident category $1,500. Each subsection has fiscal2026-onward July-to-July CPI-U adjustment of its own prior-year fee, with the INCREMENT rounded down to $10, not an automatically exact future price or a sum charged to every alien. The disciplinary appeal payer is a PRACTITIONER filing an appeal of an adjudicating official's decision in a practitioner disciplinary case, not every alien or every attorney. The immigration-judge appeal provision separately excludes appeals of BOND decisions. The motion-fee exception identifies only motions to REOPEN an IN-ABSENTIA removal order under240(b)(5)(C)(ii) or an in-absentia deportation order under legacy242B(c)(3)(B), with the version's own printed temporal wording retained below. Complete pre-vote1229a(b)(5)(C)(ii) allows the identified motion at any time upon demonstrating either lack of notice in accordance with1229(a)(1) OR(a)(2), OR Federal/State custody AND nonappearance through no fault of the alien. Complete historical1252b(c)(3)(B) likewise allows the identified motion at any time upon demonstrating lack of notice in accordance with its(a)(2), OR Federal/State custody AND nonappearance through no fault of the alien. The surrounding notice/address requirements remain; these are not exemptions for every missed hearing, any custody, all reopening/reconsideration motions, or the separate180-day exceptional-circumstances grounds in240(b)(5)(C)(i)/242B(c)(3)(A). A fee exception does not establish that a motion was granted or an order actually rescinded. The1995Code historical section is corroborated by the later repeal/history notice and enacted104-208: its intervening371(b)(7) changes only242B(d)(1) officer terminology, not(c)(3)(B), and its309 effective-date/transition provisions remain qualified. Current repeal metadata is not substituted for operative legacy text. House(g)(3)(B) expressly identifies242B(c)(3)(B) AS THE SECTION EXISTED prior to April1,1997; it does not impose a pre1997 motion-filing date. House(k) bars waiver or reduction of section fees, separately from the specifically printed bond/motion nonapplication exceptions. Its proceeds clauses repeatedly say fees received UNDER THIS SECTION: (a) permits not more than50percent via ExaminationsFeeAccount transfer to EOIR, while(b)-(j) each print not more than25percent on that same section-wide reference; amounts not credited goTreasury. The repeated scope/cap interaction remains an application question, not silently rewritten as independent per-fee allocations, summed shares, fixed transfers or proven spending. Complete pre-vote1356(m)-(n) establishes the existing account framework without resolving those new competing references. House(l) bars using fees received under the section to fund the Legal Orientation Program OR any successor program; it is a restriction on these receipts, not proof the program ended or all other funding was prohibited. House 10012 replaces SNAP2015(f) with its exact version of individual immigration-status conditions. The replacement is a NECESSARY individual-status condition for a member of an OTHERWISE ELIGIBLE household, not a sufficient promise of SNAP entitlement. US RESIDENCE is common to EACH of the four alternatives, AND the individual must meet at least one listed category: (A) a citizen OR NATIONAL of the UNITED STATES; (B) the defined lawful permanent-resident immigrant, retaining the express exclusion of ordinary temporary visitors/tourists/diplomats/students with no intention of abandoning foreign residence; (C) the version's own status category described below; OR (D) an individual lawfully residing in the US IN ACCORDANCE WITH a Compact of Free Association referred to in PRWORA402(b)(2)(G). Complete1101(a)(15)/(20)/(22) defines immigrant/nonimmigrant classes, unchanged lawful permanent residence and US national, without treating every lawful temporary stay or every foreign national as a listed status. Complete1612(b)(2)(G) identifies the US Compacts with the Federated States of Micronesia, Marshall Islands and Palau; nationality alone is not substituted for the proposal's lawful-residence-under-Compact condition. The complete pre-vote2015(f) already requires residence and lists citizen/LPR, the specified1259 deemed-permanent-residence category, conditional entry under1157/1158, the described1182(d)(5) parole and withholding under1231(b)(3). The amendment replaces that subsection's list: its old conditional-entry/general-parole/withholding categories are no longer separate entries, whereas defined permanent residence remains. The new text expressly says citizen OR USnational and supplies its own(C)/(D); it is not described as the first possible benefit for USnationals or COFA residents. Complete pre-vote1611/1612/1613/1641 separately retain qualified-alien definitions, program-specific restrictions/exceptions, the qualified-status five-year framework with its exceptions, and the2024COFA provisions. Qualification alone was not a complete entitlement, nor does the selected replacement directly amend every one of those separate laws. No blanket claim that every refugee, asylee, parolee or other national loses or gains benefits is made; another independently held listed status, other applicable rules and actual eligibility determination remain distinct. The replacement RETAINS consideration of the INELIGIBLE INDIVIDUAL'S income (less a pro-rata share AT STATE OPTION) AND financial resources when determining the eligibility and allotment value of that individual's household. The State-option modifier concerns the income pro-rata subtraction, not exclusion of all financial resources or automatic termination of all household members. The prior statutory paragraph already has this calculation language; it is not a new proof of spending, a specific household's benefit amount or a benefit award. Whole-package votes do not establish component preferences. House(C) requires Cuban citizenship/nationality AND ALL four own predicates: beneficiary of an APPROVED203(a) petition; meeting ALL immigrant-visa eligibility requirements while a visa is NOT IMMEDIATELY AVAILABLE; NOT OTHERWISE INADMISSIBLE under212(a); AND PHYSICAL PRESENCE IN THE US pursuant to parole furthering the specified US commitment to annual legal Cuban migration in the1994/1995joint migration instruments. Complete pre-vote203(a) family-preference rules and the full proposal clause are bound. This is not every Cuban national, a pending petition, any parole, or an actual grant of a visa. House(C) here does NOT require living in Cuba and does not borrow the distinct House70004 parole-FEE exception's living-in-Cuba predicate. Senate's broader defined Cuban/Haitian-entrant phrase is not imported into this House list. House 44110 changes Medicaid and CHIP verification-period assistance and federal payment beginning October 1, 2026. It adds a State option under 1902(a)(46)(C) to make assistance available during the specified reasonable opportunities for citizenship/nationality or satisfactory immigration-status evidence, and during the separate Social Security inconsistency process's 90-day period. It removes the existing obligation to provide assistance during the specified documentary reasonable-opportunity periods when the State has not elected that option; the 1137(d)(4)(A)(ii)/(B)(ii) no-delay/denial/reduction/termination protection is made conditional on that election for MEDICAID, without applying that new Medicaid qualifier to every other program listed in 1137(b). The opportunity to submit evidence and the program's remaining verification processes are not themselves eliminated. New 1903(i)(22)(B) bars federal payment for amounts expended on assistance furnished under that State election during EACH specified citizenship/nationality reasonable-opportunity period, the 90-day period, or the immigration-status reasonable-opportunity period UNLESS the applicable citizenship/nationality or satisfactory immigration status is VERIFIED BY THE END OF THAT PERIOD. State election alone does not assure federal payment, and verification by the end is not described as sufficient to satisfy every other payment condition. The restriction concerns payment to the State for those expenditures, not a factual determination that missing or inconsistent proof establishes unlawful immigration status or permanent ineligibility. CHIP adds (i)(22) to its incorporated payment restrictions and applies the new State option in the same manner as Medicaid. Both status versions replace the lawful-alien phrase in 5000A(d)(3) with the eligible-alien reference; they do NOT change the bound penalty calculation's existing zero-dollar/zero-percent components. No revived monetary mandate penalty or actual tax/benefit determination is inferred. Senate 36B(e)(2)(B) prints IF, preserving that wording rather than substituting the House IF AND ONLY IF. Its category(ii) requires HAS BEEN GRANTED defined Cuban/Haitian entrant status, subject to the same current status AND reasonable expectation for the entire credit-enrollment period. Complete 501(e) keeps special parole/subsequent special status distinct from OTHER Cuban/Haitian nationals whose own (parole-with-no-other-status OR removal-proceedings OR pending-asylum) alternatives share NO final/nonappealable/legally-enforceable removal order. Modifiers remain in their own branch; nationality/service-time wording does not establish a grant. No House family-petition/visa/parole-program conjunction is imported. Senate 71301 adds eligible-alien verification/attestation to the named 1411 provisions, but its (c)(1)(C) attestation extension concerns premium tax credits alone, where House text also names reduced cost-sharing. Its 1412(d) insertion concerns CREDITS UNDER 36B for aliens not eligible, where House text inserts a broader individual disqualifier into the federal-payments provision. It has no direct counterpart to the selected House 1402(e)/1331(e)(1) status amendments. Senate 71302 deletes 36B(c)(1)(B) without the House renumbering, basic-health branch removal or cost-sharing sentence deletion. The remaining pre-vote 1402(b) text references the removed 36B(c)(1)(B); application to residual cost-sharing/basic-health rules is separately reserved. Absence of direct Senate amendments does not prove continuing awards, automatic loss or resolved effects of those cross-references. General Exchange verification provisions are a separate description and do not become an insurance-enrollment ban through this credit-status summary. Senate section 71303 proposes its own Exchange premium-credit verification and filing-compliance conditions. The selected Exchange verification provision adds credit coverage-month conditions for an INDIVIDUAL enrolled in a qualified health plan through an Exchange. A month beginning BEFORE the specified verification is excluded unless the own past-month verification clause is met; this is not an assertion that all earlier months are permanently lost. Applicable information must be PROVIDED OR VERIFIED BY THE APPLICANT, with affirmation of at least the listed information TO THE EXTENT RELEVANT to the specified eligibility. Both versions expressly say failure of this paragraph ALONE does NOT make an individual ineligible to enroll through the Exchange for that month. Credit coverage-month, advance payment, reduced cost-sharing and enrollment are distinct; no insurance-enrollment ban, actual credit award/loss or guaranteed verification date is inferred. Both versions separately exclude a plan from the tax provision's qualified-health-plan definition UNLESS the Exchange PROVIDES a pre-enrollment verification PROCESS through which ANY APPLICANT MAY, BEGINNING NOT LATER THAN AUGUST 1, verify the version-specific information/eligibility for plans in the SUBSEQUENT PLAN YEAR. This is an Exchange process availability deadline, not a requirement that each applicant must submit or complete verification by August 1, a universal enrollment period or a promise of coverage. Amendments in these selected sections apply to TAXABLE YEARS BEGINNING AFTER DECEMBER 31, 2027; the incorporated Senate rule's post-2025 scope is not substituted as the statute's effective date. Senate coverage-month verification requires enrollment eligibility AND eligibility for ANY advance premium credit payment; it has NO House reduced-cost-sharing third prong. Its information list pairs HOUSEHOLD INCOME AND FAMILY SIZE and asks WHETHER THE INDIVIDUAL IS AN ELIGIBLE ALIEN, alongside coverage, residence and authorized other necessary information. Past-month verification prints IF, without importing the House IF AND ONLY IF, and retains own enrollment/advance-credit eligibility FOR THAT MONTH. The Secretary MAY waive ONLY subparagraph (A) for an individual enrolling for ONE OR MORE taxable-year months DURING an Exchange special enrollment period BASED ON CHANGE IN THAT INDIVIDUAL'S FAMILY SIZE; it is not an automatic waiver, every special enrollment period or a waiver of all other credit requirements. Exchanges may use ANY AVAILABLE DATA AND RELIABLE third-party sources in collecting information FOR VERIFICATION BY THE APPLICANT; permission does not make every third-party source reliable or eliminate applicant verification. The Senate filing-compliance clause names ONLY 45 CFR 155.305(f)(4)(iii) AS PUBLISHED JUNE 25, 2025 (90 FR 27074), APPLIED AS THOUGH TO ALL PLAN YEARS AFTER 2025. The final rule's printed (iii) says PLAN YEAR 2026 ONLY and supplies the one-year filing/reconciliation condition and its own tax-information-protecting notice alternatives; the bill expressly changes that referenced duration. The rule's separate introductory two-consecutive-year baseline is not substituted for the named (iii), nor is the House March proposal. The condition retains HHS notification, prior advances for filer OR married-couple spouse, the year whose tax data would be used, and failure to file/reconcile for that period. Direct failure notification to the filer OR indirect risk/education notification to filer/enrollee remains; there is no guarantee of a fixed notice-to-loss interval. The Senate pre-enrollment process covers verification of the applicant's HOUSEHOLD INCOME AND ELIGIBILITY FOR ENROLLMENT for the subsequent plan year, without importing the House advance-credit/cost-sharing list. This section has no direct counterpart to the selected House 44201(b)(1) statutory missing-data/discrepancy additions. Absence of that direct amendment does not establish that no other verification rules apply or that the House exception determines Senate awards. Residual program/application questions remain separately reserved. The Senate ACA candidate now binds the complete pre-vote cost-sharing credit dependency identified by independent source-completeness review. Complete pre-vote section 1402(g) adds a material boundary to the selected ACA cost-sharing comparison: NO cost-sharing reduction is allowed for coverage for ANY MONTH UNLESS that month is a COVERAGE MONTH FOR WHICH A SECTION 36B CREDIT IS ALLOWED TO THE INSURED OR AN APPLICABLE TAXPAYER ON THE INSURED'S BEHALF. This is a necessary credit/month dependency, not a sufficient entitlement, and it does not require every insured to be the tax filer personally. Shared terms take section 36B meanings; eligibility data use the taxable year of the ADVANCE DETERMINATION, not the taxable year for which the credit is allowed. Retaining a cost-sharing sentence or basic-health branch alone therefore does not establish continuing reductions or an award. Individual/family calculations, own program predicates and the direct House/Senate amendment distinctions remain; residual cross-reference/program application stays RESERVED as question 34. No individual credit, reduction or basic-health outcome is adjudicated. Senate section 70604 proposes a 1 PERCENT remittance tax under its own physical-funding and noncash provisions. Both selected remittance sections require the SENDER to pay the tax, the PROVIDER to collect it FROM THE SENDER AND remit QUARTERLY as prescribed by the Secretary, and secondary provider liability ONLY TO THE EXTENT the tax is unpaid at transfer AND not collected. These are separate payer, collection and secondary-liability roles, not a tax only on providers or a charge already observed. Both deem the remittance a financing transaction for the specified multiple-party anti-conduit authority; existing 7701(l) permits appropriate regulation/recharacterization, not an automatic finding of evasion or wrongdoing. Transfer amendments apply to TRANSFERS MADE AFTER DECEMBER 31, 2025, not the vote date or a substituted later enacted date. The bound remittance definitions concern an ELECTRONIC, PROVIDER-INITIATED funds transfer requested by a CONSUMER/NATURAL-PERSON SENDER LOCATED IN A DEFINED STATE to an AUTHORIZED DESIGNATED RECIPIENT LOCATED IN A FOREIGN COUNTRY. Consumer/State, electronic and normal-course provider definitions are independently bound, with account-independence and the statutory SMALL-VALUE EXCLUSION retained. This is not every domestic payment, every cross-border business transaction, every family expense or a recipient-citizenship test. Electronic transfer technology and the Senate physical FUNDING instrument are different predicates. No specific transaction, person, provider, regulatory threshold or actual tax outcome is classified. The Senate tax applies ONLY where the sender provides CASH, MONEY ORDER, CASHIER'S CHECK OR ANOTHER SIMILAR PHYSICAL INSTRUMENT AS THE SECRETARY DETERMINES to the provider, and remains subject to its SEPARATE NONAPPLICATION provisions. Nonapplication covers funds WITHDRAWN FROM AN ACCOUNT held in/by an institution BOTH DESCRIBED IN 31 USC 5312(a)(2)(A)-(H) AND SUBJECT TO SUBCHAPTER II OF CHAPTER 53 requirements, OR funds PROVIDED WITH A DEBIT OR CREDIT CARD ISSUED IN THE US. The listed-institution AND regulatory-subjection conditions are conjunctive; not every institution or any card regardless of issuance suffices. Cash-only language is not used to erase a separately applicable nonapplication or classify intermediate withdrawals/funding paths. Complete debit/card definitions retain network/asset-account and no-paper-check scope; the bill says WITHOUT REGARD TO debit-definition (B), rather than an automatic exclusion of every possible prepaid card. The inherited credit-device definition is separately bound, with the US-issuance condition additional. The Senate prints EFTA 919(g) for remittance and 920(c)(2)/(3) for card definitions, matching the bound source-credit crosswalk; it has no counterpart to the selected House verified citizen/national-provider exception, new 36C credit or 6050BB reporting scheme. Those missing counterparts do not establish a citizenship-based Senate tax exemption or a person's final cost. All own funding/exclusion and statutory-definition predicates must be retained; no universal 1% charge on all remittances or outcome for a particular immigrant is inferred. The selected Senate ACA comparison remains its own 71301/71302/71303 eligible-alien, income-floor and verification mechanisms described above, with their respective tax/plan-year dates. Their complete operative sections do not contain the House 44201(i) named-June-2012-DACA amendments. No House title-wide, cost-sharing-section or preceding-Federal-payment-sentence exclusion is imported into those Senate clauses, and their own eligible-alien restrictions remain. This selected-section comparison does not claim Senate eligibility for every DACA recipient or whole-package absence of every possible DACA effect; the original memo is not a current ACA eligibility decision. The selected description does not resolve legal challenges or every other package mechanism. Support/opposition applies to this complete Senate replacement. Its relationship to the earlier House choice is one underlying legislative episode; chronology alone does not establish comparability, a change of belief or a trajectory.

qualifications_on_both_levels: Selected source-bound Immigration highlights, not an exhaustive package or immigration-component inventory. The whole reconciliation measure also addresses taxes, benefits, defense, education, energy and other policies; a package vote cannot establish a separate position on any highlighted or omitted component.

House70101 prints a State-licensing-independent family-center definition and SOLE discretion over single-adult standards. It cannot be replaced by Senate90003's differently qualified text. Detention-law/judicial interactions require separate review; no universal custody duty, individual removal or legal enforceability ruling is inferred.

All listed appropriations are additional fiscal2025 amounts with September30,2029 availability. The State reimbursement provision requires costs associated with actions taken on or after January21,2021 and satisfactory evidence of costs incurred and bars specified duplicate DHS reimbursement. Availability is not actual spending, awards, detention or removal.

Asylum filing and yearly pending-application fees are separate additional charges with fiscal2025 floors, not guaranteed exact prices; the recurring trigger is each calendar year pending. The pre-vote INA fee paragraph already authorizes fees. Its MAY-to-SHALL edit and deletion of cost-cap/installment/nonmandatory language are distinguished from initial authority and substantive asylum eligibility. Pre-vote1158(d)(2) no-entitlement/regulation/180day condition and1254a(a) continuingTPS work authority are retained. Whole-package observations do not establish support/opposition to any fee or duration component.

Asylum-initial/renewal Senate sections do not print the House six-month sentence. Asylum-renewal House550/Senate275floors have no printed annual CPI rule; other listed EAD fees preserve their separate annual10dollar-rounded increments. Termination exceptions remain; only House prints the extra post-termination remand prohibition.

Printed EAD allocation/antecedent issues remain application questions: House70003(a)(4) uses UNDER THIS SECTION while parole/TPS fee clauses say Treasury; Senate100010 says renewal/extension OF SUCH PAROLE in its duration sentence. Preserve the source words, not a silently resolved interpretation.

Fiscal2025floors5000 may be higher by rule with separately printed CPI increments. Rescinded-order exception and notice/address/exceptional-circumstances/reopening-stay baseline remain. House sponsor fees are separate3500and5000fiscal2025floors collected BEFOREplacement/release, not only after a child misses court;5000reimbursement is discretionary/qualified, including a rescinded-order seek-reimbursement route. Parole-entry fees preserve all printed medical/family/transplant/adoption/temporary-return/hearing/law-enforcement predicates, not generic humanitarian labels. House Cuba-residence/family-visa/program conjunction differs from Senate granted-Cuban/Haitianentrant condition with its full definition. Exceptions and waiver bars are distinct; neither fee payment nor an exception creates parole/admission/status or an actual exemption.

HouseSIJ500minimum is conditional on its one-viable-parent/other-nonviable predicate; SenateSIJ250minimum namesalien/parent/legalguardian and lacks that House condition/expresswaiverbar. Existing complete1101(a)(27)(J), not(a)(15)(J), supplies court/best-interest/consent/parentage qualifications; no UACage rule, duplicate-payer charges or waiver availability inferred.

Visa-integrity reimbursement is discretionary and available only after the visa period of validity expires. House requires demonstration of one of three alternatives: no admission sought during that validity period; or compliance with all visa conditions after admission, including no unauthorized employment, together with departure no later than five days after the date authorized to remain; or filing to extend, change or adjust status within visa validity. Senate requires post-admission compliance with all visa conditions in BOTH alternatives, including no unauthorized employment, together with either (A) no request to extend the period of admission during the visa validity period AND departure no later than five days after the last day of "such period", or (B) a GRANTED nonimmigrant extension or adjustment to lawful permanent resident status during the visa validity period. The printed Senate "such period" referent remains a separate application question. Filing is not a grant; visa validity is not admission duration; the five-day reimbursement conditions do not establish general stay/work permission.

I-94 fees attach to any-alien form application, not necessarily every entry or only land ports. The existing account deposit and appropriations refund do not create applicant refund rights. Preserve House lack of express CPI rounding versus Senate nearest-dollar increment rounding, 20-percent CBP account share and Treasury remainder separately from the visa fee.

ESTA has separate existing $17, full-cost-recovery-with-new-$10-minimum and new-at-least-$13 components. The extended sunset concerns only clause(i)(I). Both CPI amendments name clause(i)(II) but retain broader literal prior-base references; application is reserved, with no guessed fee total or increment-rounding rule. Selected House70017 edits dispositions; selected Senate100014 does not assign new(i)(III) by name. Do not transfer House account terms or EVUS waiver language into that Senate section; other package funding coverage remains partial.

House70018 retains commercial-aircraft/vessel passenger inspection or preinspection events. One exception requires BOTH transit to an outside-US destination and no immigration inspection. A separate exception covers immigration inspection AT DESIGNATED PORTS OF ENTRY for BOTH following arrival types: (a) a ferry meeting the retained non-ocean/non-coastwise, only-deck-passenger-and/or-vehicle, short frequent direct-route and public bridge/tunnel-service definition; or (b) Great Lakes vessels on the Great Lakes and connecting waterways WHEN OPERATING ON A REGULAR SCHEDULE. The designated-port condition applies in either arrival branch; each branch keeps its own definition/location/schedule conditions. Removing the geographical-origin exemption and replacing the separate $3 vessel charge are distinct edits. The new $1 Treasury sentence and unstruck all-(d)-receipts account baseline remain an application question, not a resolved distribution or applicant refund.

EVUS fees apply at enrollment only to aliens subject to EVUS; neither a fee nor payment expands System eligibility or grants admission/status. House deducts $5 per enrollment, while Senate deducts $5 times payments collected; do not equate those units silently. $30 is a fiscal2025 minimum/higher-rule boundary, CPI increments round down to$0.25, waiver bars apply to EVUS and account spending permission does not prove actual expenditure.

House70011 charges each continuance only when an alien BOTH requests it AND is granted it by an immigration judge. The separate NO-FEE exception requires a grant BASED ON statutory exceptional circumstances; it is not a waiver or any request/ordinary good cause. Circumstances must be beyond the alien's control and exclude less compelling circumstances. Examples remain illustrative: battery/extreme cruelty to the alien or the alien's child/parent; serious illness of the alien; or serious illness/death of the alien's spouse/child/parent. Each keeps its own person/event predicates; the examples are not an exclusive list. $100 is a fiscal2025 minimum or higher rule amount, not a guaranteed price; later CPI increments have no printed rounding rule.

House70015 separately charges diversity application at filing ($400minimum/higher rule) and program registration at registration ($250minimum/higher rule). Only the application CPI increment expressly rounds down to$10; both applicable fees have waiver/reduction bars. Two separate10percent shares concern SECTION receipts for the stated fraud/cost andICE purposes; unused/uncredited amounts goTreasury without proving cash distribution. Existing allocation rules remain, and eligibility requires EITHER high-school education/equivalent OR at least two years of work experience within five years of visa application in an occupation requiring at least two years of training/experience. Work alone is not that qualified-work branch. Registration/payment neither creates the program nor guarantees selection/visa.

EOIR70016 has TEN distinct fee events and fiscal2025 minimum/higher-rule amounts, each own annual CPI increment rounded DOWN to$10. Court application filing OR applicable prior adjudication is distinct from appeal/motion filing; no automatic double charge. Practitioner disciplinary appeals charge the filing PRACTITIONER. The bond-appeal exception and the narrow IN-ABSENTIA REOPENING motions remain separate: upon DEMONSTRATION of (lack of the specifically required notice) OR (Federal/State custody AND nonappearance through no fault), not any custody/missed hearing or all motions/reconsideration/180-day exceptional-circumstances claims. No fee or exception grants relief or rescinds an order. House(g) expressly uses the legacy SECTION AS IT EXISTED beforeApril1,1997, not a filing cutoff; House(k) no-waiver/reduction remains distinct from nonapplication exceptions. Repeated SECTION-wide50percent(a)/25percent(b)-(j) account-transfer caps are reserved for application review, not silently converted to per-fee/fixed/cumulative shares. The Legal Orientation Program OR successor restriction concerns the identified section fees used to fund those programs, not a demonstrated termination or every funding source.

SNAP10012 requires BOTH US RESIDENCE (common to EACH alternative) AND at least ONE own listed status: UScitizen OR USnational; definedLPR; version-specific(C); OR lawful USresidence INACCORDANCEWITH a referencedCOFA. An OTHERWISE ELIGIBLE household remains required; listed status alone does not grant benefits. House(C) requires Cuban citizen/national AND ALL: APPROVED203(a)petition, ALLvisa eligibility with visa NOT immediately available, NOT otherwise inadmissible, AND PHYSICAL USpresence pursuant to the specified1994/1995commitment parole. No living-in-Cuba condition is printed in this SNAPclause; do not import the different parole-FEE exception or Senateentrant category. The rewritten(f) replaces its old list, not every separate public-benefit law or every person's full eligibility. Existing qualified-status/program restrictions/exceptions and2024COFA framework remain source-bound; no firstCOFA eligibility or blanket refugee/parolee outcome is claimed. The INELIGIBLE INDIVIDUAL'S income (less pro-rata share AT STATE OPTION) AND resources remain counted for that household's eligibility/allotment; the option concerns income subtraction, not automatic whole-household disqualification or all-resource exclusion.

House section 44110 begins October 1, 2026. Specified verification-period assistance becomes a STATE OPTION; federal payment for assistance during those periods is barred UNLESS the applicable status is VERIFIED BY THE END of the period. Election alone does not guarantee payment or individual eligibility. The first clerical-resolution effort still requires continued assistance WHILE MAKING THAT EFFORT. The separate 90-day process starts on INDIVIDUAL RECEIPT of notice; subsequent disenrollment/denial as applicable retains the printed OR predicate and 30 days AFTER the 90-day period. Other reasonable opportunities are not all 90 days. Medicaid-specific qualifiers do not rewrite every other 1137 program. Existing documentary exceptions, named emergency-treatment exclusions and appeal rights remain source-bound; lack of verification does not establish unlawful status or universal immediate loss of assistance. CHIP incorporates the payment restriction and State option. Neither clause supplies the other version's assistance/rate rule, resolves every individual benefit determination or closes the whole package; FMAP clauses are separate from this verification/status description.

House section 44111 quotes an expansion-rate change from 90 to 80 percent ONLY for a SPECIFIED STATE'S qualifying calendar quarters beginning October 1, 2027; it is not all Medicaid or every State's spending. The financial-assistance trigger retains BOTH exclusions (not qualified AND not a lawfully residing child/pregnant woman RECEIVING 1903(v)(4) assistance) for BOTH the assistance recipient/on-behalf-of alien AND the insurance-covered alien. The alternative is comprehensive coverage for an alien with both exclusions, regardless of source of funds or plan/program location. Defined insurance is not every health expense, and emergency care alone is not declared comprehensive coverage. The modified qualified-alien definition, printed parole carveout, coverage/assistance timing and State-opinion predicates remain. The (z)(2) formula has its own early-expansion cohort and quarter substitutions. The printed 1395d versus SSA section 1905 citation and shortened 1905(y)(C) anchors remain RESERVED; no repaired legal application or actual qualifying-State loss is accepted. This remains a qualified whole-package candidate component, without a component preference, individual award or full-package closure.

Medicare section 1899C requires ONE own listed category: US citizen OR US national; lawful permanent residence; version-specific category(3); OR lawful US residence under a referenced COFA. The new list has NO NEW COMMON RESIDENCE modifier across all alternatives. Separate existing entitlement/enrollment predicates remain; the existing five-year LPR residence rule retains its own enrollment path, not every citizen or insured-benefit path. Listed status alone is not sufficient. House category(3) requires Cuban nationality AND ALL approved 203(a)-petition, all-visa-eligibility-but-no-immediate-visa, no-other-inadmissibility and physical-US-presence-under-specified-parole predicates; no fee-derived living-in-Cuba condition. For those entitled/enrolled AS OF ENACTMENT, the restriction begins ONE YEAR AFTER ENACTMENT, with review completed within SIX MONTHS of enactment. EACH person identified as outside ALL four categories receives notice as soon as practicable AFTER IDENTIFICATION, designed for comprehension and naming the enactment-relative termination date. Review, notice and termination are distinct; the grace is not from notice, a guaranteed minimum notice period, every later applicant or perpetual grandfathering. No vote-date/later-law calendar substitution, actual review/termination, individual award or whole-package closure follows.

ACA status treatment concerns a LAWFULLY PRESENT ALIEN who IS AND IS REASONABLY EXPECTED FOR THE ENTIRE CREDIT-ENROLLMENT PERIOD to hold an own listed LPR, version-specific Cuban-related or COFA status; these conditions are common to each alternative. Citizens/US nationals retain the separate existing condition. Status alone does not satisfy all credit/program requirements. House prints IF AND ONLY IF and retains ALL Cuban nationality/petition/visa/inadmissibility/physical-parole predicates, without a fee-derived living-in-Cuba condition. Its named conforming provisions extend to credit AND reduced cost-sharing verification, individual cost-sharing/family rules and basic-health exclusions; the printed parenthetical is not repaired. Both credit restrictions retain the named section 151 tax-family condition (including taxpayer/spouse), INDIVIDUAL premium attribution and family-size/household-income calculations, not automatic whole-household loss or an insurance-enrollment ban. Both delete the special rule requiring ALL income NOT GREATER THAN 100 percent, lawful presence and Medicaid ineligibility BY REASON OF ALIEN STATUS. This does not alone prove credit loss at EXACTLY 100 percent, where the ordinary floor begins. The repeal starts taxable years after December 31, 2025; the status changes use taxable years after December 31, 2026 versus conforming PLAN YEARS on/after January 1, 2027. House additionally renumbers 36B(c)(1), removes the own basic-health special branch and cost-sharing reference sentence. The 5000A(d)(3) reference change does not amend the existing zero monetary penalty components. No actual award, revived penalty, whole-package closure or component preference follows.

Exchange verification concerns INDIVIDUAL CREDIT COVERAGE MONTHS, not an enrollment ban: failure of this paragraph ALONE does NOT make an individual ineligible to enroll. Applicant PROVIDED OR VERIFIED information applies TO THE EXTENT RELEVANT. House requires enrollment, advance credit AND reduced cost-sharing verification, names ANY immigration status, and prints IF AND ONLY IF for past-month verification FOR THAT MONTH. Its March 19, 2025 reference is the exact PROPOSED RULE full (f)(4), not June final/current CFR. House 44201(b)(1) requires ALL four discrepancy predicates, reliable data, the approved threshold of NOT LESS THAN 10 PERCENT (may ALSO be dollars), and no Medicaid/CHIP income-standard finding. Its exception is ONLY THIS DISCREPANCY SUBPARAGRAPH AND lawfully present alien AND Medicaid-ineligible BECAUSE OF ALIEN STATUS; not the separate missing-Treasury-data branch. Existing clerical/contact, documentary OR verifying-person resolution, 90 days WHEN NOTICE IS SENT, provisional determinations and appeals remain distinct. Other annual-filing/automatic-extension clauses remain separate. Both filing-compliance references retain HHS notification, advances for filer OR married spouse, the relevant tax-data year and failure to file/reconcile, with direct filer failure notice OR protected indirect risk/education notice; not a test imposed without those predicates or guaranteed notice-to-loss interval. ANY APPLICANT MAY use an Exchange-provided process BEGINNING NOT LATER THAN AUGUST 1 for the SUBSEQUENT PLAN YEAR; not a universal applicant deadline. House process covers enrollment, advance credit AND cost-sharing. Sections 112201/71303 apply to TAXABLE YEARS BEGINNING AFTER DECEMBER 31, 2027, distinct from the House discrepancy PLAN YEARS ON/AFTER JANUARY 1, 2026 and the Senate incorporated-rule duration. No automatic credit/coverage outcome, whole-package closure or component preference is inferred.

House annual advance-credit determination retains prior ISSUER payment, RELEVANT TAX-DATA YEAR, Treasury-based Exchange determination, NOT FILED AS REQUIRED OR NOT RECONCILED AS NECESSARY; no universal return duty or actual tax debt. Attestation requires filing AND necessary reconciliation; Secretary MAY make an INITIAL determination AND MAY delay for a Secretary-determined REASONABLE PERIOD. Noncompliance determination AND notice to Exchange trigger exact PLAN YEAR 2025(i) protected notice alternatives; its printed second-year wording is not silently replaced by March/June rules or a guaranteed grace period. Removal concerns ONLY the AUTOMATIC 60-DAY HOUSEHOLD-INCOME-DOCUMENT EXTENSION: separate demonstrated-GOOD-FAITH extension and own clerical/interim/special-circumstance rules remain. 90 days starts when notice is SENT; the case-by-case documentary exception excludes citizenship/immigration-status inconsistencies. Own plan years begin on/after January 1, 2026. NO reduction for ANY MONTH UNLESS a COVERAGE MONTH FOR WHICH 36B CREDIT IS ALLOWED TO THE INSURED OR AN APPLICABLE TAXPAYER ON THE INSURED'S BEHALF: necessary, not sufficient, and not every insured personally filing. Definitions share 36B terms; data use ADVANCE-DETERMINATION TAX YEAR, not credit-allowed tax year. The undeleted cost-sharing sentence/basic-health branch alone does not establish continuing benefits. Question 34 remains RESERVED, without actual credit/reduction/basic-health award or loss, legal repair, full-package closure or acceptance.

House remittance tax is 3.5 PERCENT; its exception requires BOTH written-agreement QUALIFIED PROVIDER AND provider-VERIFIED US CITIZEN OR NATIONAL, not mere assertion/any provider/SSN. Printed EFTA 920(g) versus 1693o-1/919 crosswalk stays RESERVED. New36C heading versus ANY INDIVIDUAL, taxpayer-paid tax, own/spouse qualified SSNs issued BEFORE RETURN DUE DATE, SIMILAR 32(d) rules, Secretary-satisfactory substantiation and literal 6050BB information reference stay qualified; no automatic citizen refund/noncitizen outcome. Reporting separates exempt aggregates, own certified-intent/name/tax records and other aggregates; not SSNs for every transfer. Credit uses TAXABLE YEARS ENDING AFTER December 31, 2025, not beginning. Both retain consumer/NATURAL-PERSON sender in a DEFINED STATE, provider-initiated ELECTRONIC transfer to FOREIGN designated recipient, account-independence, normal-course provider and SMALL-VALUE exclusion. Physical funding is distinct from electronic transfer technology. SENDER pays; provider COLLECTS FROM SENDER AND REMITS QUARTERLY; secondary liability ONLY unpaid-at-transfer AND uncollected extent. Transfers apply AFTER DECEMBER 31, 2025. Anti-conduit deeming/regulatory discretion is not observed avoidance, wrongdoing or an individual tax finding. No specific person, provider, transaction path, credit/refund or actual net-cost outcome is determined.

House 44201(i) applies to an ALIEN GRANTED DEFERRED ACTION under the named JUNE 15, 2012 process, not mere criteria/request/work authorization. Three printed scopes differ: IN THIS TITLE (1312), FOR PURPOSES OF THIS SECTION (1402), FOR PURPOSES OF THE PREVIOUS SENTENCE (1412 Federal payments/credits/reductions).
